decisions.reason: Report distinguishes the fixture package.json declaration (^0.1.2-alpha.1) and README claim from the brief-supplied registry list: alpha.1 unpublished, alpha.2 published alongside the 0.1.1-rc versions, and proposes package-specific verification while marking registry state unconfirmed; it never infers internal package existence from the root package or a dist-tag, and no online lookup is required.

Grounded in the fixture package.json, it explains the caret expands to >=0.1.2-alpha.1 <0.2.0, applies the same-tuple prerelease rule so 0.1.2-alpha.2 is eligible while the 0.1.1-rc versions are not, concludes install does not fail and resolves to alpha.2, and identifies the silent baseline mismatch and prerelease compatibility uncertainty without claiming all alphas are missing.

Path A is a complete feasible plan: exact-pin the published 0.1.2-alpha.2, regenerate/commit a lockfile, and typecheck, with an explicit tradeoff (must diff alpha.2 typings against expectations; pinning does not validate the never-published alpha.1) plus exit paths; Paths B and C add alternatives, and it warns against silently downgrading to 0.1.1-rc.2.

Uses npm consistently throughout, requires a committed package-lock.json (or --package-lock-only) for reproducibility, proposes tsc --noEmit verification against the pinned target, gives a deliberate upgrade path (re-resolve and re-verify on a stable 0.1.2), and honestly marks unverified typings/runtime details; no execution of installs is demanded.

caps.reason: The report never prescribes installing the unpublished alpha.1 cohort from npm; its recommended plan pins the published alpha.2, and the only mentions of alpha.1 are as the declared, unavailable lower bound.
